about.what: Hand-judged More Like This cases. Each seed lists candidates graded as recommendations FOR that seed. Scored by `den-atlas rail-eval <dataset dir>` (src/raileval.rs): nDCG@10, condensed nDCG@10, P@10, bad@10, judged@10, against /index/similar and a plot-only control.

grades.good: Someone who liked the seed for what makes it distinctive would plausibly want this next: the same story engine, subject or sensibility, not just the same genre label.
grades.ok: Defensible but not what the seed is: the same genre and register telling a different story; the same subject in a different register, audience or form (documentary, soap, remake); a remake or franchise entry that adds little.
grades.bad: Shares a surface label at most. Wrong audience, tone or world, or unrelated. A viewer would read it as a mistake in the row.

basis.known: Judged from what both titles are: premise, form, tone, audience. The judge's knowledge of the works, not the dataset's labels, so the set does not grade the ranker by its own features.
basis.maker: Shares a director, creator or writer with the seed. A fact, but the grade is still on the work: a maker's weaker or unrelated film is not automatically good.
basis.issue: Named as wanted or unwanted in den-atlas #23/#24 or in rail-ab's WANTED/UNWANTED lists, and the grade agrees unless a note says otherwise.
basis.triplet+: The twin positive for this anchor in den-dataset data/eval/triplets-final.json (two blind judges agreed on a shared premise). A premise twin is not always a good next watch, so the grade is judged again.
basis.triplet-: The hard negative for this anchor in the same file: an unrelated premise that looks confusable. Graded again for the same reason.

about.pooling: Candidates are the union of the first 12 of /index/similar and of the plot-only control on dataset 5b1c3213b6a1, plus titles the judge expected and neither arm surfaced. Titles the judge did not know well enough were left unjudged rather than guessed.
about.adding: Run with RAIL_EVAL_UNJUDGED=10 to print the unjudged titles in either arm's first ten as paste-ready lines. Add a grade and a basis and put the line in that seed's `judged`. A new seed needs its `split` from den-dataset scripts/v2/split.py (`half('tv:1438')`, dataset key form); the test re-derives it and fails on a mismatch. Correct a judgement by editing it in place; add a `note` when the reason is not obvious.
